## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tidyr, stringr, readr)
here::i_am("06_Composition/01_fibre_type_export/a_script/01_fibre_type_export.qmd")
```

## Read the report

FibeRtypeR (Van der Stede et al. 2026, J Physiol 604:2624) estimates the slow and fast fibre
fractions of a biopsy by deconvolution: it treats each sample's profile as a mix of reference
profiles for pure slow and pure fast fibres and solves for the proportions. It asks for label-free
quantification (LFQ) intensities and normalises them itself.
Its authors found quantification from unique peptides the most accurate.

The upload is DIA-NN's `Genes.MaxLFQ.Unique`: MaxLFQ intensities from gene-specific peptides, as
the app asks. MaxLFQ combines peptide ratios between runs into one abundance per gene and run.
DIA-NN normalised these values across runs, and the app normalises again.

```{r read}
metadata <- read_csv(here("00_Input", "metadata.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
report <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(
  here("00_Input", "report.parquet"),
  col_select = c("Run", "Genes", "Genes.MaxLFQ.Unique")
)
head(report, 3)
```

## Prepare gene values

The report has one row per precursor, and the gene value repeats on every precursor row of that
gene, so `distinct()` keeps one copy. DIA-NN writes 0 on rows whose precursor is not unique to the
gene, so 0 means not quantified and is dropped.

The search FASTA lists 43 human proteins twice, because the appended cRAP database repeats them;
MB, CKM, FABP3 and CYCS are among them. Their `Genes` reads like `MB;cRAP-MB`, and DIA-NN writes 0
in both of its MaxLFQ columns for them in every run, so this filter drops them. `01_filter.qmd`
repairs them at precursor level for the main analysis, and the next section fills them from those
repaired estimates.

Runs match `metadata$run` ignoring case, as in `01_filter.qmd`. That absorbs `Cl_MDR_7E-T2`,
written `CL_MDR_7E-T2` in the sheet, and drops the discarded S08 injection, which has no
`sample_id`. `stopifnot()` stops if any sample still holds two values for one gene.

```{r lfq}
lfq <- report |>
  filter(nzchar(Genes), Genes.MaxLFQ.Unique > 0) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(sample_id = metadata$sample_id[match(tolower(Run), tolower(metadata$run))]) |>
  filter(!is.na(sample_id))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(select(lfq, sample_id, Genes)))
head(lfq, 3)
```

## Reshape for upload

`pivot_wider()` turns the long table into one row per gene and one column per biopsy, with the
first column named `identifier` as the app expects. Columns follow the metadata order. Genes not
quantified in a sample become `NA`.

```{r upload}
upload <- lfq |>
  select(identifier = Genes, sample_id, Genes.MaxLFQ.Unique) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample_id, values_from = Genes.MaxLFQ.Unique) |>
  select(identifier, all_of(metadata$sample_id))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(upload$identifier), ncol(upload) == nrow(metadata) + 1)
upload[1:3, 1:4]
```

## Fill the cRAP-duplicated genes

The genes DIA-NN zeroed come from limpa's protein estimates instead, which the stage 01 repair
covers. The two sit on different scales, so for each sample limpa's log2 values are shifted by the
median difference from DIA-NN's log2 MaxLFQ over the genes both quantify, then back-transformed.
A gene with several protein groups uses the one with the most observed precursors. A cell stays
blank where limpa observed no precursor of that protein in that sample, matching how DIA-NN leaves
unquantified cells.

```{r fill}
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
crap_genes <- report |>
  filter(str_detect(Genes, "cRAP-")) |>
  distinct(Genes) |>
  pull(Genes) |>
  str_split(";") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_subset("^cRAP-", negate = TRUE) |>
  setdiff(upload$identifier)
observed <- rowSums(proteins$other$n.observations)
representative <- tibble(row = seq_along(observed), gene = proteins$genes$Genes, observed) |>
  filter(!is.na(gene)) |>
  slice_max(observed, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = gene)
limpa_log2 <- proteins$E[representative$row, metadata$sample_id]
rownames(limpa_log2) <- representative$gene
shared <- intersect(upload$identifier, representative$gene)
dia_log2 <- log2(as.matrix(upload[match(shared, upload$identifier), metadata$sample_id]))
offset <- apply(dia_log2 - limpa_log2[shared, ], 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)
fill_genes <- intersect(crap_genes, representative$gene)
filled <- 2^sweep(limpa_log2[fill_genes, , drop = FALSE], 2, offset, "+")
filled[proteins$other$n.observations[representative$row[match(fill_genes, representative$gene)],
  metadata$sample_id] == 0] <- NA
upload <- bind_rows(upload, as_tibble(filled, rownames = "identifier"))
c(filled_genes = length(fill_genes), not_in_limpa = length(setdiff(crap_genes, fill_genes)))
fill_genes
```

## Summary

Genes and samples in the file, the share of blank cells, and genes quantified in every biopsy.

```{r summary}
values <- as.matrix(upload[-1])
c(
  genes = nrow(upload), samples = ncol(values),
  pct_blank = round(100 * mean(is.na(values)), 1),
  complete_genes = sum(rowSums(is.na(values)) == 0)
)
```

## Save results

`fibertyper_input.csv` is the only CSV output, because the app reads nothing else. Missing values
stay blank.

```{r write}
write_csv(
  upload, here("06_Composition", "01_fibre_type_export", "c_data", "fibertyper_input.csv"),
  na = ""
)
```
